originating_prompt:
Follow-up on the Surzion storefront redesign (the Claude Design canvas https://claude.ai/artifact/1NngWusZ35X5XXWaYoSuQr is the reference — Home, Sign-in/Register, Become a partner, My partner account, Checkout). Partners are social-media CREATORS whose followers claim their code; there is no commission. Delegate pages to the smart-page-designer (run the smart-page-reviewer on every page you change), transaction work to the transaction-designer and business-logic code to the business-logic-coder (with review). Keep the checkout block's `promo` setting and surz_discount's join to SURZ_PARTNER exactly as they are. If the platform genuinely cannot do something below, say so plainly in the final report instead of faking it with a static picture or hard-coded text. Ask me only if it is really ambiguous; otherwise choose and list your choices at the end.

1. SITE HEADER (surz_site_header). It was hand-edited outside this agent (column widths, ghost badges, `showSignup: false` on auth_menu, logo maxWidth 150). Review those edits against the canvas header and keep or correct them so the header matches it: logo left; menu Home, Shop, About, Online catalogue, Partners; on the right search, Sign in / account menu, wishlist and cart. The cart and wishlist must be ICON + COUNT only — use the new `"iconOnly": true` on `cart_badge` and `wishlist_badge` (see the smart-pages skill), ghost style, with labels "Cart" / "Wishlist" kept as their accessible names. Keep the "Catalogue" download button. Run the reviewer on the header.

2. CREATORS WITHOUT A CUSTOMER ACCOUNT. Today a creator sees their referred orders only if SURZ_PARTNER.REGISTRY_ID is set, and approval fills it from a customer record with the same email. An application is made by a signed-in user, so the application row is already stamped with the applicant's own account. Make approval (surz_partner_approve) use the applicant's own REGISTRY_ID from the application first, and only fall back to the customer-by-email match when it is empty; grant the partner role to that account. Make sure surz_partner_order (referred orders, row security on PARTNER_REGISTRY_ID) then shows the creator their orders even if they never bought anything. Report how many existing partner rows lack a REGISTRY_ID and fill them where the stamp allows; do not invent accounts.

3. DESIGN PIECES NOT BUILT YET — build them with real blocks:
   a. My partner account (surz_partner_portal): the account SIDEBAR from the canvas — My account, My orders, Wishlist, Addresses & payment, Partner account (current), Sign out — beside the content, stacking above it on a phone. And a STATUS filter (All / Paid / Pending / Delivered) on the "Orders claimed with my code" list, if the list/embed supports one.
   b. Become a partner (surz_partner_register): the "Applying as <the signed-in user's email>" strip above the application form with a "Not you?" link to sign in again (only when signed in). Show the PLATFORM choice as chips (the field's `radio` edit_mask) rather than a dropdown, if the form renders radio that way; otherwise keep the dropdown and say so.
   c. Home hero (surz_home): the floating "Best seller" product card over the hero picture (product picture, "Best seller", name, price) — bound to a real best-selling product from the product master, not typed in.
   d. Product cards (home grid, shop, online catalogue, category pages, "often ordered with"): show the crossed-out MRP beside the price with "N% off" — use the new card `compareAtPrice` (bind `card.compareAtPrice` to the product's MRP column, same price format as the price) and `"showSavings": true`.

At the end list every change per page/object, what the reviewers reported, and anything you could not do.
result_summary:
on that partner's existing referred orders, where it was empty. Without this, orders placed before approval would never show to the creator.
- New orders already take `PARTNER_REGISTRY_ID` from the partner's `REGISTRY_ID`. `surz_partner_order` is keyed on that column, so a creator who never bought anything sees their orders.
- The partner role is granted to that same account.
- Existing partner rows: there is 1 (PRT00001), and it already has a `REGISTRY_ID`. Nothing was missing, so nothing was filled and no accounts were invented.
- The 2026-10-08 error about `surz_discount` having no `partner_id` column no longer applies; the live table has the column. `surz_discount`'s join to `SURZ_PARTNER` and the checkout `promo` setting are untouched.

**3. Design pieces**
- **3a. My partner account (`surz_partner_portal`):**
  - The sidebar is built as a 260px column beside the content, which should stack above it on a phone.
  - Its links are My account, My orders, Wishlist, Addresses & payment and Partner account (current item). Addresses & payment points at the My account page, because links can't target a section anchor.
  - Not built: the Sign out link, because no documented block or click action does it. The account menu in the header has Sign out.
  - Not built: the All / Paid / Pending / Delivered filter. The orders list is an embed that filters on one column only, and those options mix payment status (`PENDING`) and order status (`NEW`, `CANCELLED`).
- **3b. Become a partner (`surz_partner_register`):** no change.
  - "Applying as <email> · Not you?" isn't possible. No documented binding gives a page the signed-in visitor's email, and I didn't want to hard-code it.
  - Platform chips aren't possible either. The field's `radio` mask renders as plain radio inputs, not chips. I checked the designer preview code, not the live embed, so confirm in the workbench. The dropdown stays, and no model change is needed.
- **3c. Home hero (`surz_home`):** the "Best seller" card is bound to the active product whose ribbon is "Best Seller", sorted by `SORT_ORDER`, limit 1. Today that is Artery Forceps Crile.
  - Pages can't rank products by sales, so this is not "most sold". The ribbon is a stored product flag.
  - The card can't float over the hero picture itself. It sits in a second column with a negative top margin, so it only roughly matches the canvas position. Check it in the preview.
  - The tag reads "Best Seller", as stored, not "Best seller".
- **3d. Product cards:** `card.compareAtPrice` is bound to `MRP`, with `showSavings: true` and `MRP` added to each data source's columns. It's on `surz_home`, `surz_shop`, `surz_online_catalogue`, `surz_cat_general`, `surz_cat_dissecting` and `surz_cat_orthopaedic`.
  - Not done: the "often ordered with" strips on the ~24 `surz_p_*` product pages. They are three typed-in cards each, with hard-coded prices. Adding MRP there means typing prices, which I didn't want to do.

**Reviewer results (8 pages):** the home, shop, online catalogue and three category pages passed.
- `surz_site_header` passed with one warning: `auth_menu` on an external page. I accepted it, since the header's account menu depends on it.
- `surz_partner_portal` passed with one warning: embeds on an external page. I accepted it, since the embeds ask visitors who aren't signed in to sign in.
- The approval code had a manual review only. `requirement_doc.md` doesn't exist in this project, so there was no FRS to update.

**Choices I made**
- Kept `showSignup: false`.
- Used the ribbon flag for "best seller".
- Left the product-page strips and the platform dropdown as they are.
- Left the portal's Sign out link and status filter out rather than faking them.

**Open questions**
1. Should I convert the "often ordered with" strips on the `surz_p_*` pages into data-bound lists, so they can show MRP and savings?
2. For the partner orders list, do you want two separate filters, Payment and Delivery, instead of one combined status filter?
